value.body: The Combined Medical Services (CMS) Examination, held by UPSC, recruits MBBS doctors to central government medical posts. Posts include General Duty Medical Officer in the Central Health Service, Assistant Divisional Medical Officer in the Railways, and General Duty Medical Officer in the New Delhi Municipal Council and Municipal Corporation of Delhi.

items.label: Exam stages
items.note: 250 marks per paper; 100 for the personality test

items.label: Upper age limit
items.value: 32 years (35 for Central Health Service GDMO)

items.label: Vacancies
items.note: Railways ADMO posts were the largest group (450)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: MBBS — final-year students who have taken the final written and practical exams may apply and show proof later. Apply when UPSC notifies the exam, usually early in the year. Paper 1 covers General Medicine and Paediatrics; Paper 2 covers Surgery, Gynaecology & Obstetrics, and Preventive & Social Medicine. Shortlisted candidates face a personality test.

value.title: At a glance
items: Vacancy numbers change every year, so the level of competition changes too.
These are general-duty entry posts; specialist posts in central services usually need a PG degree and are recruited separately.
Posting depends on the service allotted — Railways, central health services or Delhi municipal bodies.

value.title: UPSC CMS vacancies by exam year
value.note: Figures as first notified. UPSC can revise them later — the 2025 count was reportedly raised from 705 to about 844. Check each year's UPSC notification.
value.source: UPSC CMS notifications, as compiled by coaching-site vacancy tables
